question: At an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305) initially certified after July 15, 2001, what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for children 6 weeks to 24 months of age? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: TABLE 3A (For centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001) Age of Children Minimum Number of Staff to Children Maximum Number of Children in a Group 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8 24 months to 36 months of age 1:5 10 36 months to School-Age School-Age 1:10 1:15 20 30
notes: Table 3A also sets a maximum group size of 8 for this band. Centers first certified on or before July 15, 2001 may use Table 3B instead (1:4 for 6 weeks to 30 months). In a mixed-age group the ratio for the youngest child applies unless the center may use the Mixed-Age Ratio Table (16 or fewer children).

question: At an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305) initially certified after July 15, 2001, what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for 3-year-olds (the rule's band of 36 months to school-age)? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: TABLE 3A (For centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001) Age of Children Minimum Number of Staff to Children Maximum Number of Children in a Group 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8 24 months to 36 months of age 1:5 10 36 months to School-Age School-Age 1:10 1:15 20 30
notes: The rule groups 36 months to school-age together (maximum group 20). School-age means eligible for kindergarten or above by the first day of the current school year. Table 3B (older centers) uses 1:10 for 30 months to school-age.

question: At an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305) initially certified after July 15, 2001, what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for 4-year-olds who are not yet eligible for kindergarten? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: TABLE 3A (For centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001) Age of Children Minimum Number of Staff to Children Maximum Number of Children in a Group 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8 24 months to 36 months of age 1:5 10 36 months to School-Age School-Age 1:10 1:15 20 30
notes: 4-year-olds fall in the 36 months to school-age band (maximum group 20).

question: At an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305) initially certified after July 15, 2001, what is the minimum staff-to-child ratio for school-age children (eligible for kindergarten or above)? Answer as the number of children per staff member.
quote: TABLE 3A (For centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001) Age of Children Minimum Number of Staff to Children Maximum Number of Children in a Group 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8 24 months to 36 months of age 1:5 10 36 months to School-Age School-Age 1:10 1:15 20 30
notes: Maximum group size 30. Table 3B (centers first certified on or before July 15, 2001) also sets 1:15, group 30, for school-age.

question: At an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305) initially certified after July 15, 2001, what is the maximum number of children in a group of 4-year-olds who are not yet eligible for kindergarten?
quote: TABLE 3A (For centers initially licensed after July 15, 2001) Age of Children Minimum Number of Staff to Children Maximum Number of Children in a Group 6 weeks to 24 months of age 1:4 8 24 months to 36 months of age 1:5 10 36 months to School-Age School-Age 1:10 1:15 20 30
notes: Group size may be exceeded on field trips, outdoor play, planned large group activities, napping and eating (OAR 414-305-0400(7)(c)); ratios still apply.

question: What is the minimum age for a teacher at an Oregon certified child care center (OAR 414-305)?
quote: A certified child care center's teachers must: (a) Be at least 18 years of age;
notes: Aides also count as staff in the ratio tables (OAR 414-305-0400(6): 'The number of teachers and aides ... is determined by the number and ages of the children'). An aide I may be 14 (OAR 414-305-0350(2)(a)) but if under 18 must stay within sight and sound of a teacher or aide II and is never left alone with children; an aide II must be 18.

question: Under Option A of Table 1 (Director Qualifications) for Oregon certified child care centers, what minimum step in the Oregon Registry must the center director have attained?
quote: TABLE 1: Director Qualifications Director Qualifications Have at least the qualifications in A, B, or C: A. At least Step 9 in the Oregon Registry
notes: Option A is one of three. Option B: 1 year as a Certified Family provider (single center with capacity of 20 or fewer). Option C: management/supervision knowledge plus child development knowledge (credits, training hours, or 600 hours of experience). The director must also be at least 21 (OAR 414-305-0320(6)(a)).

question: How many clock hours of formal training or education must each director, teacher, and aide II at an Oregon certified child care center complete annually?
quote: Each certified child care center director, multi-site coordinator, teacher, and aide II must have at least 15 clock hours of formal training or education annually related to child care, of which at least 8 clock hours is in child development and 1 hour is in health, safety, and nutrition (HSN).
notes: At least 8 hours must be child development and 1 hour health, safety, and nutrition. Staff employed less than a year: prorated at 1.25 hours per month worked. Substitute teachers/aide IIs working 240+ hours a year also need 15 hours.

question: What is the minimum activity space per child required at an Oregon certified child care center?
quote: A certified child care center must have a minimum of 35 square feet of activity space per child.
notes: Single-use areas (kitchens, hallways, restrooms, storage, offices) and space under non-child furniture are excluded; cribs count if the space under them is accessible to children.

question: What is the minimum outdoor activity space per child at an Oregon certified child care center, counted per child using the space at one time?
unit: square feet per child using the space at one time
quote: A certified child care center must provide an outdoor activity space of no less than 75 square feet for each child using the space at one time, unless a certified child care center only provides drop-in care
notes: Measured per child using the space at one time, not per licensed capacity. Centers that only provide drop-in care are exempt.

question: What is the maximum temperature of the water at handwashing sinks in an Oregon certified child care center?
quote: A certified child care center must have handwashing sinks that: (a) Have hot and cold running water; ... (d) Have water that does not exceed 120°F;

question: Before an Oregon certified child care center gives a child any prescription or non-prescription medication, what must it have on file?
answer: A signed, dated, written authorization from the child's parent
quote: Before a certified child care center gives a child any prescription or non-prescription medication, including, but not limited to, pain relievers, cough syrup, and nose drops, the center must: (a) Have a signed, dated, written authorization by the parent(s) on file
notes: Phone authorization is allowed for a single dose of non-prescription medication if the date and time are documented and the parent signs at pick-up. For chronic conditions, permission may cover up to 12 months. The medication must also be in its original labeled container (1030(1)(b)).

question: How often must an Oregon certified child care center practice evacuation drills?
quote: A certified child care center must practice evacuation drills monthly and one other aspect of the emergency plan every other month
notes: Drills must vary in days and times and be documented; another emergency-plan drill is required every other month; an evacuation drill must be held within the first 10 operating days after initial licensure. Drill records are kept at least 2 years (0250(8)).

question: How long must an Oregon certified child care center keep records that show rule compliance, such as attendance records and parent permissions?
unit: years after the record is created
quote: A certified child care center must maintain records that demonstrate compliance with all rules for 2 years following the record's creation, such as parent permissions, attendance records, emergency preparedness drills, and pet vaccinations.
notes: Staff and children's records: 2 years after employment or care ends. Records older than 1 year may be stored off site if available within 48 hours.

question: In what position must infants be placed for sleeping at an Oregon certified child care center?
answer: On their backs, on a flat, firm, non-inclined surface
quote: Infants must be placed on their backs on a flat, firm, non-inclined surface for sleeping.
notes: Infants who can roll back-to-front or back-to-side may stay in the position they assume (0630(1)(c)). Other sleep positions need a CCLD-approved exception with a medical reason and physician instructions (0630(2)).

question: By when must an Oregon certified child care center notify the Child Care Licensing Division (CCLD) of a serious injury or incident involving a child?
answer: By 5:00 pm the next business day
quote: A certified child care center must notify CCLD by 5:00pm the next business day of the following items: ... (j) Any serious injury or incident involving a child;
notes: Deadline is to the licensing agency. 'Serious injury or incident' is defined in OAR 414-305-0100(50) (e.g., injury requiring surgery). Parents must be notified immediately of an injury that may need evaluation by a physician (0270(5)(g)).

question: By when must an Oregon certified child care center have a child's immunization record (or exemption) on file?
answer: Before the child's first day of attendance
quote: A certified child care center must obtain the following information for each child, in paper or electronic format, prior to the first day of attendance that includes the parent's signature: ... (h) Immunization record or exemption that is updated when the child receives additional vaccines
notes: Immunizations need not be documented for children enrolled in a public or private elementary school (0225(1)). Children in foster care or experiencing homelessness may be served while parents work to comply (0225(2)).

question: What is the minimum number of people with current first aid and pediatric CPR certification who must be present at an Oregon certified child care center at all times, during transportation, and on field trips?
quote: A certified child care center must ensure that at least one person who has current certification in first aid and Pediatric Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is present in the center at all times, during transportation, and on field trips.
notes: Separately, all staff and substitutes except cooks must obtain first aid and pediatric CPR certification within 90 days of hire (OAR 414-305-0370(3)(a)).

question: How far apart must cribs, portable cribs, or play yards be placed when in use at an Oregon certified child care center?
quote: Be placed at least 2 feet from other cribs, portable cribs or play yards when in use that allows for a direct, unobstructed passage to each child;
notes: Applies to infant cribs, portable cribs and play yards. Cots and mats: at least 2 feet apart if children are placed head to toe, otherwise 3 feet (OAR 414-305-0900(3)(d)).

question: For how long is a regular certification for an Oregon certified child care center valid?
quote: A regular certified child care center certification is valid for no more than 1 year.
notes: Temporary certification: no more than 180 days in any 12-month period (0140(3)(b)). Renewal applications are due at least 30 days before expiration.

question: During rest time at an Oregon certified child care center, when there are no infants in the group and all children are going to sleep, asleep, or waking up, what is the minimum number of staff who must supervise the area where the children are resting (assuming enough staff are on site to be summoned)?
quote: One teacher, aide II, or aide I, with CBR enrollment, may supervise the area where children are resting if: (A) There are no infants in the group; (B) All children are in the process of going to sleep, asleep, or in the process of waking up;
notes: The room must be arranged so all children are supervised and enough staff must be on site to restore ratio. If two or more children are restless, vocal, off their cot or mat, sitting up, or interacting, the full ratio applies (0400(7)(b)).

question: An Oregon certified child care center may use the Mixed-Age Ratio Table (instead of meeting the ratio for the youngest child in a mixed-age group) when the number of children on site, or its licensed capacity, is at most how many children?
quote: A certified child care center may operate within the ratio and group size in the Mixed-Age Ratio Table when: (a) There are 16 or fewer children on site; or (b) The certified child care center's licensed capacity is 16 or fewer children.
notes: Otherwise a mixed-age group must meet the ratio and group size for the youngest child in the group (0400(11)).

question: At an Oregon certified child care center with a licensed capacity of less than 100 children, how much time must the director be on site?
answer: At least one-third of the weekly operating hours or 40 hours per week, whichever is less
quote: If a center's licensed capacity is less than 100 children, the director must be on site a minimum of one-third the weekly operating hours or 40 hours per week, whichever is less, as documented by the center.
notes: Centers over 100 children: at least half the weekly operating hours or 40 hours, whichever is less, and the director may oversee only one center (0320(3)). A director or substitute director must be on the premises during all hours of operation (0320(5)).

question: Within how many days of hire must staff at an Oregon certified child care center (other than cooks) have current first aid and pediatric CPR certification?
quote: A certified child care center's staff and substitutes, with the exception of cooks, must: (a) Have current certification in first aid and pediatric CPR within the first 90 days of hire.
notes: Online CPR training only counts if it includes hands-on instruction.

question: During which activities may an Oregon certified child care center exceed its maximum group size?
answer: Field trips, outdoor play, planned large group activities, napping and eating
quote: A certified child care center may exceed maximum group size on field trips, outdoor play, planned large group activities, napping and eating.
notes: Only group size may be exceeded; staff-to-child ratios still apply (apart from the rest-time exception in 0400(7)(a)).
